items.title: Build a Production Pipeline Live: Raw Files to a Medallion Lakehouse in 60 Minutes
items.author: codebasics
items.summary:
Raw data rarely arrives ready for analysis. The medallion architecture gives your data pipeline a clear structure, moving data step by step from raw ingestion to clean, business-ready tables.

In this live session, we will explain what the bronze, silver and gold layers are and why the split exists. We will show you how to build bronze and silver layers with Delta tables in Databricks, then build gold tables and make your pipeline safe to re-run.

items.title: The Posthuman Workforce: Why AI Agents Need a New Kind of Governance
items.author: Redpanda Data
items.summary:
AI agents aren't software, and they aren't employees. They're a category organizations have never had to manage before. One that fails in unfamiliar ways, moves at machine speed, and executes instructions without the hesitation or pushback organizations have always structurally depended on from people.

The instinct is to make agents themselves safer, however, new research argues that is necessary but not sufficient: agents lack the developmental architecture that makes human judgment reliable, and no amount of training installs it after the fact.

Watch Redpanda CTO Tyler Akidau and INVERSELF cofounders Kymberly Lasser-Chere and Chris Pollitzer as they discuss what a century of workforce governance gets right, where that playbook breaks down completely for agents, and what to build instead.

items.title: Your AI Can Click “Buy.” Should It?
items.author: AAIF Live
items.summary:
Your AI agent can read your inbox, plan your trip, and act through your browser. But when it uses your login, how much access should it really have?

In this episode of Debug Mode, we unpack agent identity, permissions, and the challenge of giving AI more responsibility without handing it the keys to everything. Through a fictional finance agent named Ryan, we explore prompt injection, why an agent’s intent matters, and what fraud detection could teach us about safer AI systems.

Then we get practical: daily briefings across email and messaging apps, using chat as a control center, planning a trip to Japan, and tackling German paperwork. Along the way, we ask where convenience becomes risk—and when a human should still make the final call.
